title: For Valorant, use tracking as support work rather than the core of the routine
summary: Tracking can still improve raw mouse control for tactical shooters, but if Valorant is the main game it should usually be supplementary work behind smaller flicks, target switching, and click-timing precision.
why: Viscose explicitly frames reactive tracking as generally useful, but says if Valorant is all you play your time may often be better spent elsewhere.

When tactical-shooter players do use tracking, the best value usually comes from manageable control or precise-tracking work that improves reading and correction quality rather than extreme reactive spam.
actions: Keep tracking to a smaller support slot in a Valorant routine instead of making it the main block.
Favor precise or control-oriented tracking families such as Snake Track, Raw Control, or manageable reactive-control variants.
Use tracking to clean correction quality and reading, then spend the larger share of the routine on smaller flicks, switching, and click timing.
avoid: Do not assume the hardest reactive tracking scenario is the best Valorant transfer just because it looks intense.
Avoid building a full Valorant playlist around tracking if your click timing and small-flick finish quality are still weaker.

drills.label: Precise tracking support block
drills.reason: Readable pace changes make it easier to build correction quality that can support tactical-shooter aim.

drills.label: Control tracking support block
drills.reason: Control-oriented tracking helps clean direction-change handling without turning the task into reactive panic.

evidence.claim: If Valorant is all you play, more reactive tracking may not be where most of your time should go.
evidence.excerpt: If Valorant is all you play, for example, your time might be better spent elsewhere.

evidence.claim: Snake Track and Raw Control are useful tracking families because they keep readable pace changes and correction discipline in the task.
evidence.excerpt: Voltaic describes Snake Track and Raw Control as precise/control tracking families centered on readable pace shifts and disciplined contact.
